definitions.gloss: cheap item; low-quality goods; bargain stuff
definitions.explanation: An inexpensive item, typically implying poor quality. Often used with a negative connotation to suggest something is cheaply made or not worth buying.

examples.japanese: これは{安物|やすもの}だからすぐ{壊|こわ}れる。
examples.english: This is a cheap item, so it breaks easily.

examples.japanese: {安物|やすもの}の{傘|かさ}はすぐに{壊|こわ}れてしまう。
{安物|やすもの}{買|か}いの{銭|ぜに}{失|うしな}いという{言葉|ことば}があるように、{安|やす}いものには{理由|りゆう}がある。
examples.english: As the saying 'buy cheap, lose money' goes, cheap things come cheap for a reason.

notes:
Composed of {安|やす}い (cheap) + {物|もの} (thing). Almost always carries a negative nuance — it does not simply mean "inexpensive" but implies low quality. The word is commonly used when criticizing the quality of goods.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安物|やすもの}の{服|ふく}: cheap clothes
- {安物|やすもの}の{時計|とけい}: cheap watch
- {安物|やすもの}{買|か}いの{銭|ぜに}{失|うしな}い: penny wise, pound foolish (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {格安|かくやす}: bargain-priced — neutral or positive, emphasizing good value
- {粗悪品|そあくひん}: shoddy goods — more formal and strongly negative
- お{買|か}い{得|どく}: good deal — positive connotation, emphasizing value

CULTURAL NOTE:
The proverb {安物|やすもの}{買|か}いの{銭|ぜに}{失|うしな}い is widely known and means buying cheap things ends up costing more in the long run, equivalent to the English "buy cheap, buy twice."
